# google_design_center_policy

A policy within an application template.

## Example Usage - Designcenter Policy Basic


```hcl
data "google_project" "project" {
  project_id = "my-project-name"
}

resource "google_design_center_policy" "example" {
  project              = "my-project-name"
  location             = "us-central1"
  space                = "example-space"
  application_template = "example-template"
  policy_id            = "example-policy"
  display_name         = "Example Policy"
  description          = "Managed by Terraform"
  policy_type          = "COMPLIANCE_FRAMEWORK"
  policy_uri           = "projects/${data.google_project.project.number}/locations/global/frameworks/builtin-us-data-boundary"

  apply_conditions {
    condition_key   = "environment"
    condition_value = "PRODUCTION"
  }

  apply_conditions {
    condition_key   = "criticality"
    condition_value = "MISSION_CRITICAL"
  }

  cloud_control_configs {
    cloud_control = "projects/${data.google_project.project.number}/locations/global/cloudControls/builtin-cloud-logging-storage-locations"

    parameters {
      key   = "cloudLoggingStorageLocations"
      value = jsonencode(["us-central1", "us-east1"])
    }
  }

  cloud_control_configs {
    cloud_control = "projects/${data.google_project.project.number}/locations/global/cloudControls/builtin-big-query-regulatory-settings"

    parameters {
      key   = "framework"
      value = jsonencode("US_REGIONAL_DATA_BOUNDARY")
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `policy_type` -
  (Required)
  Required. The type of the policy.
  Possible values are: `COMPLIANCE_FRAMEWORK`.

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the policy.

* `space` -
  (Required)
  The space in which the policy is defined.

* `application_template` -
  (Required)
  The application template to which the policy belongs.

* `policy_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID of the policy.


* `policy_uri` -
  (Optional)
  The URI of the policy.

* `policy_revision_uri` -
  (Optional)
  The revision URI of the policy.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. The display name of the policy.

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. A description of the policy.

* `apply_conditions` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. Conditions under which this policy applies. A condition uses
  the `criticality` and `environment` parameters of the application
  template.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_apply_conditions).

* `cloud_control_configs` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. Input only. Parameter values for the cloud controls of the
  policy's framework, grouped by cloud control. The API only honors them
  when framework parameter support is enabled for the project, and then
  validates them with Compliance Manager. The API doesn't return them, so
  Terraform can't detect drift on this field.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_control_configs).

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_apply_conditions"></a>The `apply_conditions` block supports:

* `condition_key` -
  (Required)
  The key of the parameter for the condition.

* `condition_value` -
  (Required)
  The value of the parameter for the condition.

<a name="nested_cloud_control_configs"></a>The `cloud_control_configs` block supports:

* `cloud_control` -
  (Required)
  The resource name of the cloud control that these parameter values
  apply to, in the format
  `organizations/{organization}/locations/{location}/cloudControls/{cloud_control}`
  or `projects/{project_number}/locations/{location}/cloudControls/{cloud_control}`.

* `parameters` -
  (Optional)
  Parameter values for this cloud control.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters).


<a name="nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters"></a>The `parameters` block supports:

* `key` -
  (Required)
  The key of the parameter.

* `value` -
  (Optional)
  The value of the parameter, as a JSON-encoded string. Use `jsonencode()` to set it.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/spaces/{{space}}/applicationTemplates/{{application_template}}/policies/{{policy_id}}`

* `name` -
  Identifier. The name of the policy.

* `create_time` -
  Output only. The time the policy was created.

* `update_time` -
  Output only. The time the policy was last updated.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


Policy can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/spaces/{{space}}/applicationTemplates/{{application_template}}/policies/{{policy_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{space}}/{{application_template}}/{{policy_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{space}}/{{application_template}}/{{policy_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import Policy using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    location = "<-required value->"
    space = "<-required value->"
    application_template = "<-required value->"
    policy_id = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_design_center_policy.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import Policy using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/spaces/{{space}}/applicationTemplates/{{application_template}}/policies/{{policy_id}}"
  to = google_design_center_policy.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), Policy can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_design_center_policy.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/spaces/{{space}}/applicationTemplates/{{application_template}}/policies/{{policy_id}}
$ terraform import google_design_center_policy.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{space}}/{{application_template}}/{{policy_id}}
$ terraform import google_design_center_policy.default {{location}}/{{space}}/{{application_template}}/{{policy_id}}
```
